content: 1. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is contraindicated, and alternative medications should be used. 2. Triclabendazole and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and close monitoring when co-administered. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels of trifluoperazine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 4. Lopinavir increases the levels of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 5. Both lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels of trimipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. Triptorelin increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Alternative drugs should be used. 7. Ritonavir increases the levels of tropisetron by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 8. Tucatinib increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Ritonavir increases the levels of tucatinib through other mechanisms, and co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 10. Tucatinib increases the levels of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates where small concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. 11. Ublituximab reduces the effects of ritonavir through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 12. Lopinavir increases the levels of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 13. Ritonavir decreases the levels of ubrogepant by increasing its metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 15. Lopinavir increases the levels of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 16. Lopinavir increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used. 17. Ritonavir increases the levels of upadacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 19. Lopinavir increases the levels of valsartan by decreasing hepatic clearance. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Ritonavir increases the levels of vamorolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The starting dose of vamorolone should be reduced to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. 21. Lopinavir and vandetanib both prolong the QTc interval, increasing toxicity. Alternative drugs should be used. 22. Lopinavir increases the levels of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 23. Ritonavir increases the levels of vemurafenib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative drugs should be used. 24. Ritonavir increases the levels of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase. 25. Ritonavir increases the levels of venlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 27. Ritonavir increases the levels of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 28. Ritonavir increases the levels of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used, and the daily dose of vilazodone should be reduced to 20 mg. 29. Ritonavir increases the levels of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 30. Ritonavir increases the levels of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 31. Ritonavir increases the levels of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 32. Ritonavir increases the levels of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 33. Ritonavir increases the levels of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 34. Lopinavir increases the levels of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 35. Ritonavir decreases the levels of voriconazole by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 36. Ritonavir increases the levels of vortioxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used, and the dose of vortioxetine should be reduced by 50%. 37. Ritonavir decreases the levels of warfarin by increasing its metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 38. Ritonavir increases the levels of zileuton by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 39. Ritonavir increases the levels of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 40. Ritonavir increases the levels of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 41. Ritonavir increases the levels of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 42. Ritonavir increases the levels of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 43. Common side effects of ritonavir and lopinavir include diarrhea, hyperlipidemia, nausea, rash, abdominal pain, elevated liver function tests (LFTs), headache, weakness, hyperuricemia, flatulence, and neutropenia. Rare but severe reactions include Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, and hypersensitivity reactions. 44. Ritonavir and lopinavir are contraindicated with certain drugs, including alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonists (e.g., alfuzosin), antiarrhythmics (e.g., amiodarone, flecainide), rifampin, voriconazole, and ergot derivatives. 45. Pregnant women taking ritonavir and lopinavir have not shown treatment-related malformations in animal studies, but embryonic and fetal toxicities occurred at maternally toxic doses. 46. HIV-infected mothers are advised not to breastfeed to prevent postnatal transmission of HIV and potential adverse effects in the infant. 47. Ritonavir and lopinavir are protease inhibitors that prevent the formation of mature, infectious viral particles by inhibiting the cleavage of Gag-Pol polyprotein precursors. 48. Ritonavir enhances the action of lopinavir by inhibiting its metabolism, thereby increasing serum concentrations and prolonging its effect. 49. Ritonavir and lopinavir tablets can be taken with or without food, while the oral solution should be taken with food. 50. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommend that HIV-infected mothers avoid breastfeeding to prevent postnatal HIV transmission and adverse effects in the infant.
